description: Stats track only, no audio. Each case lists the delivered report snapshots, the tap track, the mute changes and the end of the call, and the expected stats intervals (the 'intervals' columns of the stage 3 files), the deliveries that are dropped (index in the list, rule) and, for n_chunks consecutive probe chunks [t_media + 32 ms i, t_media + 32 ms (i + 1)) (t_media_ns is the tap clock at media start), the five stats flags and 'overdue' (released as an unknown chunk) as runs of ones [first chunk, count], and the release clock of each chunk as runs [first chunk, count, release_ns]. The inputs are fed to the streaming rule in event order (RX blocks, mutes and deliveries by time, then the end of the call); the flags of a chunk are the flags at its release. A null counter is an absent field. Times are int64 ns; req_ns, arrive_ns and oldest_ns are on the tap clock; report_ns is on the UTC clock and is used only to drop a repeated delivery. A case may also list inputs that reach the engine late or never ('late', with the hold 'reorder_hold_ns' at the top): the stored flags are then those of the stream fed that way, and the intervals those of the inputs in order.

cases.name: steady
cases.description: no anomaly: every interval known, the reference for the other cases; the two guard intervals close the ends

cases.name: first_burst_before_sample
cases.description: the first request is at 1.000 s and audible concealment runs from 0.960 to 0.990 s, just before the first sample (about 1.003 s): it is in the baseline of the counters and in no delta, and the sample is only known to lie in [req - 50 ms, arrive]. The guard interval [0.950, arrive_0) is unknown, so the chunks inside it are concealment-unknown (without it interval 1 would call them clean)

cases.name: first_sample_late
cases.description: the first request is at 1.000 s but the worker thread samples at 1.800 s (callback 1.815 s); audible concealment 1.1 to 1.5 s is in the baseline, in no delta. Guard interval [0.950, 1.815) unknown (interval 1 spans it and is known)

cases.name: last_callback_late
cases.description: the track ends at snapshot 24 (request 24.5 s, sampled 24.502 s) and its callback runs 1.2 s after the request (below late_ms); audible concealment 24.3 to 24.9 s is partly after the last sample, in no delta. Guard interval [24.450, arrive_24) unknown, and nothing is known after it

cases.name: worker_busy
cases.description: the worker thread is busy for 0.4 s at snapshot 10: request 10.5 s, counters sampled at 10.9 s, callback 10.915 s. Audible concealment 10.65 to 10.85 s lies before the sample, so it is counted in interval 10, whose span runs to the callback: the interval end is the arrival, never the request or a report timestamp

cases.name: join_foreign
cases.description: the request at 8.5 s joins a collection that another stats caller on the same connection started at 7.8 s (that caller's request is outstanding: oldest_ns 7.8 s); the counters were sampled at 7.803 s, 0.697 s before the request, and the callback runs at 8.8 s. Audible concealment 7.9 to 8.2 s is counted in interval 9, which therefore starts at the oldest outstanding stamp (7.8 s) and not at req - cache_ms (8.45 s)

cases.name: dup_delivery
cases.description: the app's own timer fires again at 13.5 s while the collection of the request at 12.5 s is still in flight (its callback runs 1.3 s after its request): the second request joins it and is delivered right after with the same report timestamp and the same counters. The duplicate is dropped (a zero-length interval would reset the TX floor to -120 dB) and interval 13 spans from the first request to the next report: it is 2 s long, and so is its TX window (d(tx_duration_s) above tx_span_ms), so it is unknown, as with a missing report

cases.name: playout_stall
cases.description: nothing is played between the reports 12 and 13 (hold): report 13 has a new timestamp but all ten counters equal those of report 12, and the later counters lost that second; the tap counted nothing either (a gap in the tap track without a jump of its position). Not a duplicate: interval 13 is known with zero deltas

cases.name: same_report_other_counters
cases.description: reports 12 and 13 carry the same report timestamp but different counters: not a duplicate, both are used

cases.name: report_clock_step
cases.description: the UTC clock steps forward by 0.8 s at report 12 and back by 2.8 s at report 20 (report times go backwards): the report timestamp is never used for timing, so every interval, flag and column equals the steady case

cases.name: out_of_order
cases.description: the callbacks of reports 13 and 21 run before those of reports 12 and 20 (1.45 s after their requests): the file lists them in arrival order, the engine orders by request time, so the span of interval 12 (20) ends after that of the interval that follows it. Interval 12 has audible concealment and a chunk near the end of its span is touched only interval 21 (audible concealment) ends exactly at 21.500 s, so the chunk [21.600, 21.632) (widened start through it; interval 21 (audible concealment) ends exactly at 21.500 s, so the chunk [21.600, 21.632) (widened start 21.500 s) is not touched by it. The TX power is -56 dBFS except in interval 13, where it is -42.88 dBFS: the floor there is the floor after interval 12 (-54.78 dB, which rose by 1.21 dB over the 2.42 s between the arrivals of reports 11 and 12) minus 0.20 dB, because the arrival of report 13 is 0.40 s BEFORE that of report 12 (the elapsed time between arrivals is negative and the floor falls: threshold -42.98 dBFS, active); a floor that only rises (the elapsed time clamped at 0) has the threshold at -42.78 dBFS and calls it inactive

cases.name: req_boundary
cases.description: request 13 is stamped exactly like request 12 (requests must strictly increase: interval 13 unknown) and request 21 one ns after request 20 (known)

cases.name: malformed_stamps
cases.description: snapshot 13 arrives one ns before its request and snapshot 17 has an oldest outstanding stamp one ns after its own request (neither can happen on one clock): both are dropped and the intervals across them are 2 s long, with a TX window of 2 s (above tx_span_ms): unknown, as with a missing report; snapshot 21 arrives exactly at its request (valid) and is kept

cases.name: echo_overlap
cases.description: the overlap of two spans puts tEnd + post_ms in two intervals with different look-backs: interval 10 has a jitter buffer delay of 1.7 s (pre 2098 ms), 9 and 11 are at the 1000 ms floor, 15 again has 1.7 s and 16 is at the floor. TX is active in interval 7 (6.6 to 7.4 s) and in interval 13 (12.6 to 13.4 s): a chunk whose end lies in the overlap of 9 and 10 (or of 15 and 16) is excluded or not by the LARGEST look-back of the two, whichever comes first

cases.name: span_edges
cases.description: spans are half-open and the widening is 100 ms: interval 9 (audible concealment) ends exactly at 9.500 s, so the chunk [9.600, 9.632) (widened start 9.500 s) does not overlap it and is clean, and interval 13 (audible concealment) starts exactly at 12.900 s, so the chunk [12.768, 12.800) (widened end 12.900 s) does not overlap it and is clean

cases.name: late_boundary
cases.description: callback 10 runs exactly 1500 ms after its request (not above late_ms: known) and callback 20 exactly 1501 ms after (unknown); each makes the next callback follow it (one thread, delivered in order) without making it late

cases.name: late_run_known
cases.description: 16 callbacks (10 to 25) each exactly 1400 ms after their request (a loaded thread): every interval is known, each spans about 2.5 s and overlaps its neighbours by about 1.5 s, so the concealment of the steady track is attributed to more chunks, never fewer

cases.name: late_run_unknown
cases.description: the same at 1600 ms (above late_ms): intervals 10 to 25 are unknown, the others are placed as in the steady track

cases.name: late_burst
cases.description: the signalling thread blocks for 2.2 s at report 14: its callback (above late_ms) is late and reports 15 and 16 are delivered one behind the other after it (1.2 s and 0.2 s after their requests: known)

cases.name: last_deliveries_swapped
cases.description: the last two reports are delivered in the opposite order: report 31 (callback 1.44 s after its request, below late_ms) arrives 0.4 s after report 32, which is the last one. Interval 31 ends at that late arrival, 32.922 s, the latest end of any interval of the track, and the guard interval after the last snapshot (report 32) ends earlier, at 32.522 s. 1040 probe chunks go past it: a chunk that ends after 32.922 s is concealment-unknown and TX-unknown, although the widening of the known interval 31 by 100 ms overlaps it (chunks 1028 to 1039). They are not covered by the intervals themselves; the widening decides overlap only, never coverage

cases.name: missing_report
cases.description: report 20 never arrives: the interval between reports 19 and 21 is [lo_19, arrive_21), 2.1 s long, inside span_ms, but the TX power it reports is an average over 2 s (above tx_span_ms): unknown. The TX power is -56 dBFS except -42 dBFS in the second between the samples of reports 20 and 21, which alone is active (threshold about -43.5 dBFS); averaged over the two seconds it is -44.8 dBFS, inactive. Without the TX window bound the interval would be known and inactive and the chunks over the burst would be neither excluded nor TX-unknown

cases.name: receiver_restart
cases.description: the inbound counters restart from zero at snapshot 15 (the receiver was re-created) while the stamps advance normally: interval 15 is unknown, interval 16 is known again

cases.name: sender_restart
cases.description: the outbound counters (energy, duration) restart from zero at snapshot 15: interval 15 is unknown

cases.name: stream_replaced
cases.description: the audio inbound-rtp row of snapshot 15 and the later ones has another SSRC (the inbound stream was replaced; the counters of a young new stream can already exceed the old ones, so no delta is negative): interval 15 is unknown, interval 16 is known again

cases.name: absent_fields
cases.description: absent counters (null): all inbound counters in the first two reports (no inbound-rtp row yet), the media source counters in report 8, and one counter (jb_emitted) in report 20: the intervals that use them are unknown

cases.name: silent_over_concealed
cases.description: delta(silent_concealed) = 480 above delta(concealed) = 0 in interval 15: doubtful, so unknown (a helper that clamps the difference at 0 would call it 0; the engine must not). Interval 18 has the two equal (silent-only concealment): known, audible 0

cases.name: tx_levels
cases.description: TX power given per interval (dBFS): the margin of 12 dB above the noise floor (-44.0 inactive, -43.0 active), the rise of the floor per second of elapsed tap time between ARRIVALS (callback 8 is 1.0 s late, so 2.0 s pass before it and about 0 s after), a loud run of six intervals, and the absolute limit of -50 dBFS (-50.5 inactive, -49.5 active)

cases.name: tx_floor_over_unknown
cases.description: the inbound counters restart at snapshot 15 (the receiver was re-created: interval 15 is unknown, interval 16 is known again; the outbound counters are untouched). The TX power is -60 dBFS in interval 14 (the floor drops to -60 dB), -47.25 dBFS in interval 16 and -56 dBFS elsewhere. The floor rises by 0.5 dB per second of elapsed tap time between the ARRIVALS of a snapshot and the one before it in request order, known or not: 1.0 s between snapshots 15 and 16, so the floor is -59.5 dB and the threshold -47.5 dBFS, and interval 16 is active. A floor that rises over the time since the previous KNOWN interval (2.0 s, floor -59.0 dB, threshold -47.0 dBFS) calls it inactive

cases.name: mute_boundaries
cases.description: the mute rules at their boundaries, with a TX burst (-42 dBFS in a track at -56 dBFS, active unless the interval is muted) in each of the intervals 6, 9, 12, 15 and 18. A mute change {t_ns, muted} is a change at that instant, and the state at an instant is that of the last change at or before it; an interval is muted when the state at its START is muted and no unmute falls strictly inside it. Interval 6: muted exactly at its start and unmuted exactly at its end (not inside it): muted, so inactive. Interval 9: muted one ns before its start and unmuted exactly at it: not muted, active. Interval 12: muted one ns after its start (the state at the start is unmuted): not muted, active. Interval 15: muted at its start and unmuted one ns after it (inside): not muted, active. Interval 18: muted at its start and never unmuted: muted, inactive

cases.name: span_bound_missing_reports
cases.description: reports 20 and 21 never arrive: the interval between reports 19 and 22 is [lo_19, arrive_22), 3.1 s long, above span_ms (2600), with a TX window of 3 s (above tx_span_ms): unknown. The TX power is -56 dBFS except -42 dBFS in the second of the missing report 21, which alone is active (threshold about -43.5 dBFS); averaged over the three seconds it is -46.4 dBFS, inactive. Without the bound the interval would be known and inactive and the chunks over the burst would be neither excluded nor TX-unknown (here either bound alone decides; span_boundary pins the span bound alone, tx_span_boundary the TX window bound)

cases.name: span_boundary
cases.description: the poll of request 10 slips to 1050 ms after request 9 and its callback runs exactly 1500 ms after the request (late_ms: trusted): the span [lo_9, arrive_10) is 50 + 1050 + 1500 = 2600 ms, exactly span_ms: known. Request 20 is 1 ns later than 1050 ms after request 19 with the same callback delay: 2600 ms and 1 ns, unknown, although its callback is not late

cases.name: tx_span_boundary
cases.description: the counters of report 10 are sampled 1749.5 ms after those of report 9 and those of report 20 1750.5 ms after those of report 19 (a worker thread that samples late; the callbacks are not late and the spans are 1.8 s): the TX power of the interval is an average over d(tx_duration_s) = 1749.5 ms (tx_span_ms 1750: known) and over 1750.5 ms (unknown). The bound is on the window of the average, not on lateness

cases.name: tx_late_known
cases.description: callback 5 runs 1450 ms after its request (trusted: below late_ms; its span is 2.5 s, below span_ms) and report 5 carries a TX burst (-40 dBFS in a track at -56 dBFS): the TX window is still the 1 s between the samples, so the interval is known and TX-active. Lateness widens the span, never the window of the TX average

cases.name: join_missed_by_registry
cases.description: as join_foreign (the request at 8.5 s joins a collection another caller started at 7.8 s; counters sampled at 7.803 s) but the app's registry did not see that caller, so oldest_ns = req_ns and the span of interval 9 starts at 8.45 s: the audible concealment 7.9 to 8.2 s is in no span that counted it. The tap tells: the received-samples counter counted 0.3 s between reports 7 and 8 where the tap counted 1.27 s, and 1.7 s between 8 and 9 where the tap counted 0.73 s, so intervals 8 and 9 are unknown

cases.name: recreated_same_ssrc
cases.description: the inbound stream is re-created at 0.9 s with the same SSRC (a young stream: its counters restart from zero, and 0.6 s later, at report 1, they are still above those of report 0, so no counter went backwards and rx_ssrc did not change): the received-samples counter counts 0.1 s between reports 0 and 1 where the tap counted 1.0 s, so interval 1 is unknown, and the offset between the counters jumped by 0.9 s; interval 2 is known again

cases.name: tap_offset_drift
cases.description: the received-samples counter counts 60 ms fewer samples than the tap from reports 6, 9 and 12 on (a counter discontinuity of 2880 samples each): one step is below the allowance of the delta check (the two spans of the interval, 20 ms of lag and 20 ms of tolerance) and of the offset check (this interval's span plus 40 ms); the second makes the offset 120 ms below the largest offset seen, so the offset check marks interval 9 unknown and restarts the bound; the third is one step again

cases.name: tap_drop_between_arrivals
cases.description: the worker queue drops the tap blocks between 14.70 s and 15.30 s (400 ms of queue overflow, 60 blocks); the tap callback counted them before the queue, so the position of the next block includes them and the span between the arrivals of reports 14 (14.53 s) and 15 (15.53 s) still holds 1.0 s: every interval is known. A port that counts the blocks it received instead sees 0.6 s too little and marks interval 15 unknown

cases.name: tap_drop_over_arrival
cases.description: the worker queue drops the tap blocks between 14.00 s and 15.05 s and report 14 arrives at 14.53 s inside the gap: the position the engine knows at that arrival is the one of the last block before the gap (14.00 s), 0.53 s too low, so intervals 14 and 15 are unknown (the tap cannot tell where it was), and so is interval 13, whose counters look 0.53 s too old next to the stale position of report 14 (the one-ahead comparison)

cases.name: tap_delta_boundary
cases.description: the received-samples counter counts more samples than the tap from report 8 on, by 9744 samples (203 ms) at report 8 and by 8689 samples (181 ms) at report 18, the largest jumps that the delta check allows there being 9744 and 8688 (the spans of the two reports and of the one before, plus 40 ms): interval 8 is known, interval 18 is unknown (one sample, 20.8 us, over). The intervals before the jumps, 7 and 17, are unknown as well: a jump this size is above what the one-ahead comparison allows (tap_ahead_boundary)

cases.name: tap_offset_boundary
cases.description: the received-samples counter counts 4848 samples (101 ms) fewer than the tap at report 8, the largest drop of the offset that the offset check allows there (the span of the report plus 40 ms): known; the offset is restored at report 9 (a gain of 101 ms is inside the delta check). At report 18 the drop is 5041 samples, one over the 5040 allowed there: interval 18 is unknown, and the offset is restored at report 19. (A drop that is not restored is tested again by every later report against the largest offset seen, with a smaller allowance each time.)

cases.name: tap_ahead_boundary
cases.description: the received-samples counter counts more samples than the tap from report 9 on, by 5088 samples at report 9 and by 5809 at report 19: the one-ahead comparison marks the interval BEFORE a jump up when the next offset exceeds this one by more than the span of this report plus 40 ms (a report whose counters are older than its bracket looks like that), the delta check the interval of the jump itself only above the spans of both reports plus 40 ms. At report 9 the jump is the largest one that keeps interval 8 known, at report 19 one sample (20.8 us) more: interval 18 is unknown; the intervals 9 and 19 are known

cases.name: tap_arrival_on_block
cases.description: reports 8 and 18 are delivered exactly on a tap block (8.600 s and 18.600 s: the callback of that block is at that instant), and the received-samples counter counts 4656 (report 8) and 4657 (report 18) samples fewer than the tap there, restored at the next report. The tap position at an arrival is the one of the last block called AT OR BEFORE it, so the block that is called at the arrival counts: 4656 samples is the largest drop the offset check allows at report 8 (known), one sample more at report 18 is unknown. A position that excludes the block at the arrival (10 ms less) or one that takes the next block (10 ms more) moves the limit by 480 samples

cases.name: tap_end_on_arrival
cases.description: the track ends at report 19, which is delivered exactly at the last tap block (19.600 s: the tap is still defined there), and the received-samples counter counts 20000 samples (0.42 s) fewer than the tap at it: the offset check and the delta check run and interval 19 is unknown. A tap that is taken as ended at its last block would skip report 19 and call it known

cases.name: tap_end_skips_predecessor
cases.description: the tap ends at 13.700 s. Report 12 is delivered 1.4 s after its request, at 13.900 s, after the end of the tap (the checks skip it); report 13 is delivered at 13.550 s, before it (the file lists it first), and the received-samples counter counts 20000 samples (0.42 s) more than the tap from report 13 on. Report 13 has no checked predecessor (the one before it was skipped, and the delta check does not look past a skipped report) and the offset check only looks for drops, so interval 13 is known. A port that compares report 13 with report 11 sees the jump and marks it unknown

cases.name: hidden_concealment_event
cases.description: an audible concealment event at 14.3 s whose samples a merge correction cancelled (the jitter buffer's negative correction after an earlier merge is subtracted from this event): concealmentEvents moves by 1, concealedSamples and silentConcealedSamples do not. Interval 14 has audible 0 and silent 0 and events 1: it touches concealment, so the chunks within 100 ms of its span are touch_conc (a rule on the sample counters alone would call them clean)

cases.name: muted_tail_hidden_event
cases.description: a long loss from 10.6 s to 12.49 s that the jitter buffer has muted (silent samples; its event is counted in interval 11) and an audible event at 12.2 s whose samples the merge correction that ended the loss cancelled: interval 12 holds the muted tail (silent samples), no new event of the loss, and the hidden event: audible 0, silent > 0, events 1. It touches concealment (a rule that lets silent samples in the interval switch the event off would call the chunks around 12.2 s clean, with the event in the same interval as the tail)

cases.name: dtx_silent_concealment
cases.description: four concealment events with silent (comfort noise) samples only, as an Opus DTX gap would produce (the apps negotiate no DTX): concealmentEvents moves and silentConcealedSamples with it, so audible is 0 and each of the four intervals still touches concealment (an event counts whatever its samples are: over-flagging a DTX gap costs availability only, missing a hidden event next to a muted tail would cost the verdict)

cases.name: late_delivery_3s
cases.description: snapshot 10 of the steady track is delivered 3.0 s after its request, behind newer snapshots (a signalling thread that blocked, or a second thread). The snapshot after it in request order, 11, has request 11.494 s, so snapshot 10 arrives more than late_ms after the request of the snapshot it would be ordered in front of (13.508 s > 11.494 s + 1.5 s): D1 drops it. The span of interval 10 is then the 2.1 s from the bracket of snapshot 9 to the arrival of snapshot 11, with a TX window of 2 s: unknown, as with a missing report. Without D1 the snapshot would be placed before its successor and the span of its own (unknown) interval would reach back over chunks that a streaming engine has already released as clean, so keeping it gives other flags for the chunks near it

cases.name: late_delivery_6s
cases.description: snapshot 10 of the steady track is delivered 6.0 s after its request, behind newer snapshots (a signalling thread that blocked, or a second thread). The snapshot after it in request order, 11, has request 11.494 s, so snapshot 10 arrives more than late_ms after the request of the snapshot it would be ordered in front of (16.508 s > 11.494 s + 1.5 s): D1 drops it. The span of interval 10 is then the 2.1 s from the bracket of snapshot 9 to the arrival of snapshot 11, with a TX window of 2 s: unknown, as with a missing report. Without D1 the snapshot would be placed before its successor and the span of its own (unknown) interval would reach back over chunks that a streaming engine has already released as clean, so keeping it gives other flags for the chunks near it

cases.name: d1_boundary
cases.description: D1 at its boundary: snapshot 10 arrives exactly late_ms (1500 ms) after the request of snapshot 11, which follows it in request order (13.010 s = 11.510 s + 1.5 s, exactly on an RX block, which is fed first): kept, with its own interval unknown (2.5 s after its request) and the intervals around it as the rule gives them; the chunks that wait for it are released at that RX block's time, 13.010 s, not at the next block. The lo of snapshot 11, 11.460 s, is exactly 100 ms past the end of chunk 354 (11.360 s): its concealment flags are final when snapshot 11 heads the horizon (H = t1 + widen_ms), its TX flags only when H is past t1 + post_ms, so the chunk is released with the next snapshot. Snapshot 20 arrives one ns later than that for snapshot 21: dropped. The comparison is strict: a delivery is dropped when req + late_ms < arrive_ns of the snapshot it would be ordered in front of. The same report delivered once more 1 ms later is dropped by D1 too: the duplicate check compares with the previous KEPT delivery, and the dropped one is not

cases.name: d2_start_before_predecessor
cases.description: D2, the start of the bracket before that of the snapshot ahead in request order: snapshot 15 carries an oldest outstanding stamp 5 s before its request (a registry entry that was never released), so its lo is far below that of snapshot 14: dropped, and interval 15 spans from the bracket of snapshot 14 to the arrival of snapshot 16 (2.1 s, a TX window of 2 s): unknown. The starts of the kept snapshots never decrease in request order, so a later interval cannot reach back over chunks that were released. Snapshot 20 has its lo exactly equal to that of snapshot 19 (an oldest stamp 50 ms before the request of 19): kept. Snapshot 24 has it one ns below that of snapshot 23: dropped

cases.name: d2_start_after_successor
cases.description: D2, the start of the bracket above that of the snapshot behind in request order: snapshot 13 joins a collection that started at 12.000 s (oldest outstanding stamp), so its lo is 12.000 s, above that of snapshot 11; snapshot 12 is delivered after 13 and has lo 12.456 s, above that of the snapshot behind it: dropped (interval 12 spans from the bracket of 11 to the arrival of 13, a TX window of 2 s: unknown; interval 13 is 2.54 s long, inside span_ms: known). Snapshot 22 is delivered after 23 with a lo exactly equal to that of 23: kept; snapshot 28 after 29 with a lo one ns above that of 29: dropped

cases.name: overdue_after_gap
cases.description: reports 20 and 21 never arrive while the RX blocks go on, and request 22 is stamped 22.550 s. The chunks that end after 18.35 s need a snapshot after the gap: snapshot 22, settled when the clock is strictly past 24.050 s (the RX block at 24.050 s does not settle it, the one at 24.060 s does), and the one before it in request order (19, which has its lo, 19.45 s, past them); until then they are not final. Each is released as an unknown chunk (excl 0, tx_unknown 1, conc_unknown 1, touch_conc 0, touch_stretch 0) at the first input with a clock at or past its end plus overdue_ms (5.5 s): chunk 574 (end 18.400 s) at the RX block of 23.900 s, with a malformed delivery one ns earlier that does not release it; chunk 578 (end 18.528 s) at 24.029 s, a malformed delivery, which moves the clock although it is dropped. Chunk 579 (end 18.560 s) is overdue at 24.060 s, the RX block at which snapshot 22 is settled: final comes first, with the flags of the intervals (it touches the concealment counted in interval 18) and release 24.060 s; so do all later chunks that end by 20.35 s

cases.name: mute_moves_clock
cases.description: the track of overdue_after_gap without the malformed deliveries, and one mute change at 24.055 s, between the RX blocks of 24.050 and 24.060 s. The clock is the time of the latest input and a mute change is an input: at 24.055 s the clock is strictly past 24.050 s, request 22 + late_ms, so snapshot 22 is settled and the chunks that wait for it (579 on: end 18.560 s and later) are final and are released then, at 24.055 s. An engine whose mute changes do not move the clock releases them at the next RX block, 24.060 s. The mute changes no flag (it falls after every interval that these chunks look at); the chunks that are overdue earlier are released at the RX blocks after their overdue time

cases.name: end_of_call_flush
cases.description: the call ends at 24.0 s, with chunks that are not final: the stats track has 22 snapshots (the last request 21.494 s, arrival 21.520 s), the RX blocks stop at 21.510 s, so the last snapshot has no block at or after its arrival and is skipped by the tap checks, and no input comes between 21.52 s and the end of the call, so no snapshot after the one ending at 19.35 s is settled. At the end every waiting chunk is released with the flags that the track gives (the guard of the last snapshot stays: unknown, and everything after the last interval is unknown), at the clock of the end of the call, 24.0 s, and none counts as overdue (the end of the call comes first)

cases.name: late_rx_arrival_on_block
cases.description: the case tap_arrival_on_block, with the RX block that is called at 18.600 s, exactly at the arrival of report 18, reaching the engine 0.2 s late, after the block of 18.610 s was fed. Report 18 was fed before the block and read the position of the block before it, one block (10 ms, 960 ticks) too low, which is inside the allowance of the offset check: fed in order, interval 18 is unknown, with that position it would be known (and 71 probe chunks would be released known clean that the feed in order releases unknown). The block is dropped; the position of report 18 is stale, so the intervals that read it are unknown: 17, 18 and 19, and the offset check from then on compares with the largest offset it has seen (it does not restart)

cases.name: late_rx_same_time
cases.description: the case late_rx_arrival_on_block with the late block reaching the engine at 18.705 s, so that the worker has fed the delivery of report 18 (at 18.600 s) and nothing after it: the clock is exactly the time of the block, and the block comes before the delivery at the same time in the feed. The block is late although its time is not below the clock; the stats track drops it and marks the intervals that read the position of the block before it, as there

cases.name: late_rx_gap
cases.description: report 18 is delivered at 18.604 s, after the RX block called at 18.600 s and before the block of 18.610 s, and the received-samples counter counts 4849 samples (101 ms) fewer than the tap there, one more than the offset check allows with this arrival (4848): unknown. A mute change at 18.602 s (to unmuted: it changes nothing) moves the clock past the block, and the block reaches the engine at 18.703 s: late. The delivery of report 18 is fed after it and before the next block, and reads the position of the block before it, 10 ms too low, which would make interval 18 known: the position stays stale until the next block is fed, so the intervals that read it are unknown although the delivery was not fed yet when the block was dropped

cases.name: late_rx_checked
cases.description: the case late_rx_arrival_on_block with the late block reaching the engine 1.8 s late (20.400 s: the worker has fed the inputs before 20.300 s) and report 19 delivered 1.4 s after its request, at 20.894 s (below late_ms), after the late block. Report 18 is checked as soon as it is settled, at 20.000 s, with the position that it read when it was fed (the block before the late one), which is inside the allowance of the offset check: interval 18, which ends at it and is not built yet (the next report is not delivered), looks known. When the late block is dropped, report 18 is stale although it is checked already, and the interval that ends at it is unknown; report 19 reads the right position, so nothing else marks it. Without that mark 21 probe chunks (552 to 572) are released known, where the feed in order releases them unknown

cases.name: late_rx_cover
cases.description: the tap ends at 21.520 s and report 21 is delivered at 21.515 s, between the blocks of 21.510 and 21.520 s. From report 21 on the received-samples counter counts 10000 samples (208 ms) more than the tap: in order the delta check marks interval 21 and the one-ahead comparison interval 20. A mute change to unmuted at 21.570 s (the state does not change) moves the clock past the last block, which reaches the engine at 21.720 s: late. It is dropped, and no block at or after the arrival of report 21 is fed after it, so that the tap would not cover the arrival and the tap checks would skip report 21 (32 probe chunks, 604 to 635, would be released known); in order the last block covers it. The late block covers the reports that arrived at or before it: report 21 is checked with the position that it read (the block before the late one, which is the right position), and intervals 20 and 21 are unknown

cases.name: late_rx_floor_rise
cases.description: a TX track at -56 dBFS with a quiet interval (-75 dBFS) at report 3 and a burst of -49.5 dBFS at report 31 (above the -50 dBFS limit, and above floor + 12 dB only while the floor is below -61.5 dB). The feed in order has the floor at -75 dB after report 3 and raises it by 0.5 dB per second over the 28 reports between, to about -61 dB: the burst is inactive. The RX block called at or just before the arrival of report 3 reaches the engine 0.2 s late: reports 2 to 4 are unknown, and from then on the TX test reads the lowest floor, which never rises (-75 dB): the burst is active and its chunks are excluded, which excludes more than the feed in order does (and not a floor that rises as the chain does)

cases.name: late_rx_floor
cases.description: the case tx_levels (the TX floor drops to -75 dBFS in intervals 13 and 15, interval 16 at -49.5 dBFS is active), with the RX block called at or just before the arrival of report 14 reaching the engine 0.2 s late. Reports 13 to 15 read a stale position, so their intervals are unknown, and the TX floor chain misses the two quiet intervals: it would stay near -55 dB and call interval 16 inactive, where the feed in order has the floor at about -74 dB and calls it active. After a late block the TX test reads the lowest floor that any feed can have (the chain over every interval with counters, in which the floor never rises)

cases.name: late_rx_offset_boundary
cases.description: the case tap_offset_boundary (the received-samples counter 5041 samples below the tap at report 18, one over what the offset check allows: unknown), with the RX block called at or just before the arrival of report 18 reaching the engine 0.2 s late. Report 18 reads the position of the block before it, 10 ms too low: the drop of the offset is then inside the allowance and interval 18 would be known. It is unknown, with the intervals next to it

cases.name: late_rx_drift
cases.description: the received-samples counter loses 3000 samples (62.5 ms) at report 10 and 1600 samples (33.3 ms) at report 11, and the RX block called at or just before the arrival of report 9 reaches the engine 0.2 s late. Fed in order, the offset is 87.5 ms below the largest offset seen at report 10 and 107.8 ms below it at report 11 (the allowances are 125 and 110 ms: known) and 125.8 ms below it at report 12 (allowance 125 ms): interval 12 is unknown. Report 9 reads a position 10 ms too low, which raises the largest offset that the check holds by 5 ms, so report 11 is 112.8 ms below it and the check, which restarts its maximum there, would judge report 12 against the restarted maximum and call interval 12 known, where the feed in order calls it unknown. From the first late block on the offset check compares with the largest offset ever seen and never restarts, so interval 12 is unknown here too

cases.name: late_unmute_0_2s
cases.description: the steady track with a TX burst at 10.42 to 10.50 s, muted from 0.2 s and unmuted at 10.400 s: the unmute reaches the engine 0.2 s late (the worker has fed everything before 10.5 s and the unmute is below the clock). It is kept at its own time and moves nothing else. The intervals that it can reach and that were built before it reached the engine are marked unknown, so the chunks that are released after it are TX-unknown instead of known clean (the interval that holds the burst counts as muted whole without it, and its chunks would be released known clean while the local user talks); the intervals built after it read it as if it had come in order; a chunk that was released before it was fed keeps its flags. At 0.2 s no interval that holds it has been built

cases.name: late_mute_0_2s
cases.description: the steady track with a TX burst at 10.42 to 10.50 s and the local user muted at 9.000 s (the intervals that start after it are muted whole, so inactive): the change to muted reaches the engine 0.2 s late. Kept at its own time, and the built intervals that it can reach are marked unknown (without the change they count as not muted and would exclude the burst's chunks, the safe direction, but a rule that treats a late unmute and a late mute alike has one shape); the intervals built after it read it normally

cases.name: late_within_hold
cases.description: inputs that reach the engine within the hold (`reorder_hold_ns`, 100 ms) are merged in their place and the stats track never sees them late: the unmute of late_unmute_2_7s reaching it 80 ms late, the RX block called at 10.000 s 90 ms late and the delivery of report 10 60 ms late. Every expected value equals the case without `late`

cases.name: lost_unmute
cases.description: the unmute of late_unmute_2_7s is lost (a bounded queue overflowed and dropped it) and the worker learns of the loss 2.7 s after its time: a lost change is a late UNMUTE at the time of the latest mute change that was fed (0.200 s), so the intervals after 0.2 s count as not muted until the next change, and the built intervals that it reaches are marked unknown. The flags are those of the feed in order or more unknown, and no chunk is released known clean over the burst

cases.name: lost_unmute_behind

The marker is a late unmute with the time of the change AHEAD of the lost one in the queue (0.200 s), not of the latest change that was fed (11.000 s): from 0.2 s the intervals count as not muted until the mute at 10.6 s, so the burst at 10.42 to 10.50 s excludes its chunks; a marker at 11.000 s leaves the state muted from 0.2 s to 10.6 s and the burst's chunks are released known clean

cases.name: lost_behind_late
cases.description: the mute at 0.200 s reaches the engine late, at 11.500 s, and the unmute at 10.400 s behind it is lost; the worker learns of the loss at 11.400 s. The marker comes through the same queue as the changes, so it is fed after the late mute ahead of it, not before: both have the time 0.200 s, the marker is behind the mute and the unmute wins, so the burst at 10.42 to 10.50 s excludes its chunks. A marker fed first would be overtaken by the late mute at the same time, and the burst's chunks would be released known clean
